question: Thanjavur Quartet is best remembered for the revival and codification of which ancient classical dance form?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thanjavur Quartet refers to four brothers—Chinnayya, Ponnayya, Sivanandam, and Vadivelu—renowned for their contribution to Bharatanatyam.
 
• They were instrumental in reviving, codifying, and systematizing Bharatanatyam as a classical art form during the early 19th century.
 
• They composed numerous dance pieces, including varnams and padams, that became integral to the Bharatanatyam repertoire.
 
• The brothers served in the court of King Serfoji II of Thanjavur and were deeply influenced by his patronage of the arts.
 
• Their efforts laid the foundation for the margam (traditional sequence of Bharatanatyam performance), which is still followed today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It combines bhava (expression), raga (melody), tala (rhythm), and natyam (dramatic art).
 
• Traditionally performed in temples as an offering to deities, it is deeply rooted in spiritual and religious themes.
 
• The dance is accompanied by Carnatic music, and its movements are characterized by intricate footwork and graceful gestures.
 
 
 
• **Thanjavur Quartet's Legacy:**
 
 
• The Quartet's compositions are still widely performed and respected in Bharatanatyam recitals.
 
• They introduced innovations such as integrating music with dance and enhancing the use of abhinaya (expressive storytelling).
 
 
 
• **Margam:**
 
 
• Margam is the traditional sequence of a Bharatanatyam performance, consisting of pieces like alarippu, jatiswaram, varnam, padam, and tillana.
 
• This structure was formalized by the Thanjavur Quartet, making it a hallmark of Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **King Serfoji II:**
 
 
• King Serfoji II of Thanjavur was a major patron of the arts, encouraging the development of Bharatanatyam under the Thanjavur Quartet.
 
• His reign saw a flourishing of Tamil classical music, dance, and literature.
